FOREWORD This Indian Standards ( Third Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau the draft finalized by the Lubricants and Related Products Sectional ved by the Petroleum Coal and Related Products Division Council. of Indian Committee Standards, had been after appro-

This standard was first published in 1953 and subsequently revised in 1970 and 1980. The present revision of this standard has been prepared as the result of a review of the standard by the Technical Committee in the light of the present day requirements and advancement in the field of lubrication technology in the country. While reviewing this standard the Committee felt that this standard as well as IS 506 : 1983 `Specification for automotive grease', which also covers two grades for defence requirements, should be rationalized on the basis of general purpose user's and defence requirements. Accordingly one grade for general user are being deleted frcm this standard ard two grades for defence requirements covered in IS 506-1983 are being added in this draft revision. With these modifications this revised standard will now be applicable only to defence requirements and requirements for other general purpose users will be separately covered under 1S 506 : 1983 which is also being revised. In preparing by Ministry this revision, assistance of Defence, UK: has been derived from Service the following standards : LG 280 published

Joint DEF STAN 91-17/l Grease, Calcium base. CS 2985 Grease LG 190, LG 280 and LG 320

Designation

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with LS 2 : 1960 &Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard
GENERAL PURPOSE GREASE FOR DEFENCE APPLICATIONS - SPECIFICATION ( Third Revision )
1 SCOPE

This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for greases intended for plain bearings and other automotive and general applications. The standard also includes applications over the ambient temperature range of - 18�C to + 60�C. 2 NORMATIVE

The use of the Standard Mark IS governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BlS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of lndian Standards.
